sample_unit: clinical notes in test splits (1048 local + 202 n2c2)

links.outcome: Comparison of candidate LLMs on the same ADE extraction data (F1)
links.effect: GPT-4o outperformed GPT-4o-mini on both datasets, with higher F1-scores (0.524 vs. 0.381) and a more balanced precision-recall profile.
links.quote: GPT-4o consistently outperformed GPT-4o-mini in ADE extraction across both datasets, with higher F1-scores (0.524 vs. 0.381) and a more balanced precision-recall profile.

links.outcome: Error types in LLM-extracted ADE relationships, including misclassification and conflation
links.effect: Both models showed limitations: misclassification of pre-existing allergies and occasional conflation of therapeutic indications with adverse effects; GPT-4o had fewer errors.
links.quote: Both models captured ADEs effectively in explicit and complex clinical contexts, although limitations included misclassification of pre-existing allergies and occasional conflation of therapeutic indications with adverse effects.

screen.reason: Retrospective benchmark evaluating multiple LLMs (GPT-4o, Llama 3.2, etc.) for adverse drug event extraction from clinical notes without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
